A phrase has an ordinary subject, object, or preposition-complement use without a separate target nominal.
An independent phrase contains a partitive of-PP.

A phrase functions as displaced subject in an existential there-construction, with dummy there as subject.
A phrase admits a modifier attached inside its own nominal projection; the query states the modifier and its position.
A phrase admits a peripheral modifier attached outside its own determiner and internal nominal dependents; the query states the modifier.
A phrase contains a comparative than-phrase complement.
A phrase functions as a degree modifier of a non-adjectival target; the query states the target category.
A phrase functions as predicative complement of a copular verb.
The phrase takes genitive marking or has a genitive form (Kim's, my/mine, whose).
The phrase controls or transmits subject-verb agreement or number (number transparency, singular/plural selection).
The phrase inflects for number (plural -s) or lacks a number contrast.
The phrase has comparative or superlative inflection or a grade paradigm (fewer/fewest, more/most, less/least).
The phrase functions as predeterminer modifier before a determined NP (all the books, both these).
The phrase functions as a marker of coordination (both ... and, either ... or, neither ... nor).
The phrase is the determinative base of a compound (anyone, something, nothing) or the claim concerns a compound's modifier domain.
The claim concerns the fused-head analysis (fused determiner-head or modifier-head) of the phrase, or an ordinary-Head versus fusion comparison.
The phrase, itself determinative-headed, takes an external determiner (the few, the lucky few, a certain, the very few).
The sentence makes a taxonomic, analytical, or methodological statement about a category or class, not a claim about a specific construction.
None of the above. Give other_label in a few words.
